summary.title: RAGU: A Multi-Step GraphRAG Engine with a Compact Domain-Adapted LLM

setting_and_object.category: System / Software artifact (with an accompanying fine-tuned model)

details: Existing GraphRAG systems build knowledge graphs in a single LLM extraction pass, yielding noisy, duplicated entities and brittle retrieval, and they default to expensive large API LLMs.

Claimed premise: the skills an in-pipeline LLM needs (comprehension, extraction, reasoning over provided context) are language skills that scale weakly with parameter count, unlike parametric world knowledge, so a compact extractor should suffice.

RAGU: an open-source, pip-installable modular GraphRAG engine whose defining design principle is separating extraction from consolidation — two-stage typed extraction (entities first, then relations constrained to validated entities under the NEREL schema of 29 entity / 49 relation types), DBSCAN-based deduplication plus LLM summarization of entities/relations, then hierarchical Leiden community detection with LLM community reports.
Meno-Lite-0.1: a 7B model fine-tuned from RuadaptQwen2.5-7B specifically for RAG language skills (context use over fact recall) to serve as the in-pipeline extraction LLM.

Explicit engineering-maturity goal: swappable three-tier storage (graph/KV/vector), async-first API, Pydantic-validated LLM outputs instead of eval(), incremental upsert/delete, ~374 tests with a mock LLM server, single-GPU deployment.
GraphRAG-Bench (Medical) with four difficulty levels: fact retrieval, complex reasoning, contextual summarize, creative generation.
Metrics: LLM-judged Answer Correctness, ROUGE-L, Coverage, Faithfulness, Evidence Recall, Context Relevancy; judge is google/gemini-3-flash-preview (disjoint from generator).
IE/KG-construction benchmark (nerel-bench): NER F1, relation extraction F1, entity/relation definition chrF++, harmonic mean; plus MERA and LIBRA passkey retrieval for the model.
All systems share gpt-4o-mini as answer generator and the same embedding model (bge-large-en-v1.5 for GraphRAG-Bench; gte-multilingual-base for multi-hop), so only the graph-construction LLM varies.
Index LLMs varied: Meno-Lite-0.1 (7B), Qwen2.5-3B/7B/14B, gpt-oss-20b.
Two answer-generation prompt protocols for multi-hop QA: each system's default verbose prompt vs. a terse single-answer prompt (HippoRAG 2 is already terse and serves as format anchor).
LightRAG and HippoRAG 2 (primary), NaiveRAG (RAGU's own NaiveSearchEngine), with Microsoft GraphRAG referenced in cost analysis.
Engineering comparison against a pinned HippoRAG 2 commit (eval() on raw LLM output, assert False control flow, concrete storage backends, no CI).

Continued pretraining on 1.3B tokens of Russian+English educational/scientific text, then SFT on 50M tokens of NEREL-based extraction, multi-hop QA, and query logs; 128K context; 47% better Russian tokenizer efficiency (3.77 vs 2.57 chars/token).
Ablations over 11 RAGU configurations toggling ICL examples (0/1), schema validation, and extractor size (3B–14B).
Cost analysis: ~8k indexing tokens/doc at ~2k tok/s, ~$0.001/doc on rented GPU vs ~$0.10/doc for gpt-4o-based MS-GraphRAG.
Qwen2.5-Instruct family (0.5B–72B) evaluated on MERA: CheGeKa (world knowledge) vs MultiQ (all facts in context).

key_findings.finding: Multi-step consolidation yields the most complete retrieved context and wins on synthesis-oriented tasks, while chain-traversal retrieval wins on single-fact precision, producing a cross-over with task complexity.
key_findings.evidence: On GraphRAG-Bench Medical, RAGU has the highest Evidence Recall at every factoid level (up to 0.84 vs ≤0.76) and highest Coverage throughout (57.4 vs 34.7 on Creative Generation); Answer Correctness gap to HippoRAG 2 shrinks monotonically from -18.2 pp (Fact Retrieval) to -14.7 pp (Complex Reasoning) to -0.9 pp (Contextual Summarize) and reverses on Creative Generation (59.0 vs 56.9 AC, 34.2 vs 26.6 Faithfulness). LightRAG is weakest at every level.

key_findings.finding: HippoRAG 2's apparent large multi-hop QA advantage is largely an answer-format artifact rather than a retrieval-quality gap.
key_findings.evidence: Under verbose default prompts HippoRAG 2 leads all columns (BioASQ AC 74.1 vs 56.0; ROUGE-L 48.8 vs 12.2). With a terse prompt forcing a single direct answer, RAGU matches or exceeds on BioASQ (72.9 vs 72.4 AC) and narrows 2WikiMultiHopQA from -19.3 pp to -5.5 pp (58.0 vs 63.5); a genuine lead remains only on MuSiQue (54.4 vs 40.1).

key_findings.finding: A 7B model fine-tuned for language skills beats much larger general LLMs at knowledge-graph construction, especially relation extraction.
key_findings.evidence: On the IE benchmark Meno-Lite-0.1 (7B) attains the best harmonic mean 0.468 vs 0.416 for Qwen2.5-32B (+12.5% relative), driven by RE F1 0.347 vs 0.239 (also above gemma-3-27b 0.224, Qwen2.5-14B 0.222); MERA score 0.555 and 0.98 passkey retrieval at 128K tokens.

key_findings.finding: Once a consolidation stage is present, end-to-end GraphRAG QA quality is largely insensitive to the extraction LLM's size or standalone extraction quality.
key_findings.evidence: Across extractors from 3B to 14B (and Meno-Lite vs Qwen2.5-7B) Answer Correctness on GraphRAG-Bench varies by at most ~1.5 pp; ICL and validation toggles each shift AC by <1 pp; Meno-Lite's large standalone extraction edge compresses to ≤1 pp downstream in RAGU, HippoRAG, and LightRAG alike; multi-hop QA differs by only 1–2 pp between gpt-oss-20b and Meno-Lite as index LLM.
